To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) materialistic media messages can cultivate self-enhancement related cognitions, and (b) chronic exposure to these media messages can cultivate anti-welfare values and support for punitive welfare policy.

“Chronic attention to materialistic media content is associated with higher levels of dispositional materialism and decreased support for welfare policies, and these relationships are mediated by self-enhancement related cognitive-affective processes”.
heavy exposure to media messages that portray wealth, fame and luxury increases support for punitive welfare policies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of materialistic media messages and the cultivation of materialistic values.
the effects of commercial television viewing on materialism and antiwelfare orientations.
the potential effects of commercial media on the development of prosocial orientations, and in turn on societal well-being.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study shows how materialism and anti- welfare orientations can be triggered by materialistic media messages.
the findings of this study provide a more detailed theoretical and experimental understanding of how commercial media may undermine prosocial development, and societal wellbeing.
the study found evidence for the cultivation of materialistic values and anti-welfare attitudes via the consumption of commercial media messages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more one watches materialistic media, the more materialistic one becomes and the less supportive of social welfare one becomes.
the more you watch commercial media, the more materialistic you are likely to become, and this may lead you to become less likely to support the welfare state and the poor.
materialistic media messages may be a significant source of socialization that can cultivate materialistic values and undermine prosocial orientations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the media is not a benign source of entertainment, but rather a powerful force that can cultivate materialistic values and anti-welfare attitudes.
media can be used to promote prosocial development and social welfare.
media messages can be powerful agents of socialization that may cultivate material values and undermine support for welfare.
